author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A man sought in a Long Island homicide investigation was fatally shot by police in Erving after authorities say he confronted officers with a knife outside a motel. Officials identified the man as 55-year-old Brandon William Hampson, who was accused of killing a former girlfriend in Sayville, New York.

Massachusetts authorities said officers located Hampson on Wednesday. According to their account, he produced a knife and advanced toward police after officers gave commands. Officers then fired, and Hampson died. The description comes from law-enforcement officials and remains subject to the review that follows a fatal police shooting.

The case connected a New York homicide investigation with a police operation in western Massachusetts. NBC10 Boston reported that authorities planned a formal update as investigators worked to establish the sequence of events and the circumstances that brought Hampson to Erving.

No officers were reported killed. Officials had not released a complete evidentiary record, including body-camera footage or a final use-of-force finding, when the update was published. Those questions will be addressed through the continuing investigation. The homicide accusation against Hampson also remained an allegation and was not adjudicated in court before his death.
dek: Massachusetts authorities say Brandon William Hampson confronted officers with a knife outside an Erving motel after investigators traced him from a New York homicide case.
headline: Long Island homicide suspect killed by police in Erving, authorities say
